title: Vyasa, born on an island
hook: a sage, a ferry and a fragrance: the birth of Vyasa, the teacher Hindus thank on Guru Purnima
carry: guru purnima thanks vyasa and every teacher

segments.voice: Yesterday: Satyavati, a king's daughter raised by the chief of the fishermen, and the epic's own teaching. Conduct, not birth, shows who you are.

Before the palace, there's a boat. Satyavati rows travelers across the Yamuna for her father, the chief of the fishermen. Ordinary work, on a wide river. One day a sage on a pilgrimage steps in and sits down. His name is Parashara. Out on the water, he looks at her, and he wants her. And the young woman holding the oar has to think fast, alone, in the middle of a river.
screen: `A FERRY ON THE YAMUNA.` → `A SAGE STEPS IN.` → `OUT ON THE WATER.`

segments.voice: The text gives Satyavati words here, and she uses them with care. There are sages on the banks, she says; they can see us. So Parashara makes a mist, and the banks disappear. Then her next worry: I'm a maiden, living under my father. What becomes of me? He answers that she'll remain a maiden, and tells her to ask something for herself. She asks for one thing: that her body, which has always carried the smell of fish, smell sweet. He grants it, and from then on, the text says, her fragrance carried far across the land. Some readers see a girl bargaining with the little power she has; some see a woman caught in a sage's power, asking what she can. The text lets her ask. On an island in the Yamuna she gives birth to a son, and before he leaves for the forest he promises her: whenever you think of me, I'll come. Hold that promise. He's called Dvaipayana, the island-born, and tradition knows him as Vyasa, the arranger. Hindus honor him as the sage who arranged the Vedas and gave the world the Mahabharata. That's why one full moon a year, in the month of Ashadha, is called Vyasa Purnima, or Guru Purnima, the teacher's full moon. On that day many Hindus thank their gurus: students bow to music and dance teachers, families visit spiritual teachers. The idea under it: what you know didn't start with you. It came down a line of teachers, and the boy born on that island stands near its head.
screen: `A MIST COMES DOWN.` · `ONE THING, FOR HERSELF.` · `A SON BORN ON AN ISLAND.` · `VYASA, THE ARRANGER.` · then, large: `GURU PURNIMA.`

segments.voice: On Guru Purnima, many Hindus bow to a teacher, with folded hands or by touching the teacher's feet. Bring to mind one person who taught you something that stayed: a grandparent, a coach, a teacher, the writer of a book. Fold your hands and bow your head a little toward them. If you pray, thank God for them; if not, just say their name and thank you.
Satyavati. The ferry girl who asked for a fragrance, and whose island-born son Hindus thank as the teacher of teachers.
Your line: Guru Purnima thanks Vyasa and every teacher. And keep his promise to his mother close. Day seven hundred seventeen, done.

screen: `DAY 717 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE PRINCE WITH NO EQUAL.`
